context.passage:
Sandwich Franchise A cquires
Technology Company

GROVE CITY (February 27)-Lunch Hut,
the national restaurant franchise known for
serving farm-to-table sandwiches, has
acquired My Handy Chef, a technology
company that manufactures a line of robots
that can perform basic kitchen tasks. My
Handy Chef cofounder Ryan Boone has
joined Lunch Hut's corporate office as an
innovation strategist, bringing with him a
team of talented engineers and designers.

The robots are skilled in mixing
ingredients for sauces and spreads as well as
peeling and chopping vegetables.

With the acquisition of My Handy Chef,

Lunch Hut's leadership team is excited to
make progress toward automating the
production of such signature dishes as their
famous Pasta with Farm Greens Pesto and
Spicy Egg Salad.

"At its best, technology facilitates
smoother human interactions, and I believe
this development will help us to do an even
better job of attending to our customers'
needs," said Eva Griffin, Lunch Hut's
longtime CEO. Lunch Hut has always been
known for the personable service of its staff
members, who assemble each custom
sandwich order by hand.

choices: It has begun producing kitchen appliances.
It has purchased Mr. Boone's company.
It has removed dishes from the menu.
